source: 10 seed-1 games, 4 computer players, politics on, trunk 2eccd439; WS5 prototype run of 6 Nov (store-pricing spec, Sim section)

charts.title: Highest Food price in any month
charts.note: The store's highest asking price over all 120 game-months. Today's prices run away; the proposal stays readable.

charts.title: Months a price sat at its ceiling
charts.note: Months, over all ten games and all goods, when a store price was at twelve times normal.

charts.title: Months colonists went short
charts.note: Of 120 game-months. Water shortages nearly halve. Food shortages rise: today's runaway prices drag Food out of players' hands into the store (657 units over the ten games, against 271), at prices nobody can plan around.

charts.title: Months the store had no Food left to sell players
charts.note: Of 120 game-months. Under every rule we tried, today's included, the store runs out of Food almost every month: the colony doesn't grow enough.

charts.title: Hungry seat-months
charts.note: Of 480 seat-months (ten games, four seats, twelve months): months a player began development with less Food than their household and crew eat. It is judged before the month's buying and after half the Food has spoiled, so a player needs about three months' Food left over to count as fed.

note: What this says. The new prices calm the market and fix Water, but no price rule can make Food appear. That is the supply decision (decision 1): bring the hardship rules in together with more Food, tuned in one pass.
